verses.1: When the king lived in his house, and Yahweh had given him rest from all his enemies all around,
verses.2: the king said to Nathan the prophet, “See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but God’s ark dwells within curtains.”
verses.3: Nathan said to the king, “Go, do all that is in your heart, for Yahweh is with you.”
verses.4: That same night, Yahweh’s word came to Nathan, saying,
verses.5: “Go and tell my servant David, ‘Yahweh says, “Should you build me a house for me to dwell in?
verses.6: For I have not lived in a house since the day that I brought the children of Israel up out of Egypt, even to this day, but have moved around in a tent and in a tabernacle.
verses.7: In all places in which I have walked with all the children of Israel, did I say a word to anyone from the tribes of Israel whom I commanded to be shepherd of my people Israel, saying, ‘Why have you not built me a house of cedar?’ ” ’
verses.8: Now therefore tell my servant David this: ‘Yahweh of Armies says, “I took you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, to be prince over my people, over Israel.
verses.9: I have been with you wherever you went, and have cut off all your enemies from before you. I will make you a great name, like the name of the great ones who are on the earth.
verses.10: I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place and be moved no more. The children of wickedness will not afflict them any more, as at the first,
verses.11: and as from the day that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel. I will cause you to rest from all your enemies. Moreover Yahweh tells you that Yahweh will make you a house.
verses.12: When your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will set up your offspring after you, who will proceed out of your body, and I will establish his kingdom.
verses.13: He will build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
verses.14: I will be his father, and he will be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men and with the stripes of the children of men;
verses.15: but my loving kindness will not depart from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away before you.
verses.16: Your house and your kingdom will be made sure forever before you. Your throne will be established forever.” ’ ”
verses.17: Nathan spoke to David all these words, and according to all this vision.
verses.18: Then David the king went in and sat before Yahweh; and he said, “Who am I, Lord Yahweh, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
verses.19: This was yet a small thing in your eyes, Lord Yahweh, but you have spoken also of your servant’s house for a great while to come; and this among men, Lord Yahweh!
verses.20: What more can David say to you? For you know your servant, Lord Yahweh.
verses.21: For your word’s sake, and according to your own heart, you have worked all this greatness, to make your servant know it.
verses.22: Therefore you are great, Yahweh God. For there is no one like you, neither is there any God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
verses.23: What one nation on the earth is like your people, even like Israel, whom God went to redeem to himself for a people, and to make himself a name, and to do great things for you, and awesome things for your land, before your people, whom you redeemed to yourself out of Egypt, from the nations and their gods?
verses.24: You established for yourself your people Israel to be your people forever; and you, Yahweh, became their God.
verses.25: “Now, Yahweh God, the word that you have spoken concerning your servant, and concerning his house, confirm it forever, and do as you have spoken.
verses.26: Let your name be magnified forever, saying, ‘Yahweh of Armies is God over Israel; and the house of your servant David will be established before you.’
verses.27: For you, Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, have revealed to your servant, saying, ‘I will build you a house.’ Therefore your servant has found in his heart to pray this prayer to you.
verses.28: “Now, O Lord Yahweh, you are God, and your words are truth, and you have promised this good thing to your servant.
verses.29: Now therefore, let it please you to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever before you; for you, Lord Yahweh, have spoken it. Let the house of your servant be blessed forever with your blessing.”

verses.1: But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time, he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time he has made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
verses.2: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. The light has shined on those who lived in the land of the shadow of death.
verses.3: You have multiplied the nation. You have increased their joy. They rejoice before you according to the joy in harvest, as men rejoice when they divide the plunder.
verses.4: For the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, you have broken as in the day of Midian.
verses.5: For all the armor of the armed man in the noisy battle, and the garments rolled in blood, will be for burning, fuel for the fire.
verses.6: For a child is born to us. A son is given to us; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
verses.7: Of the increase of his government and of peace there shall be no end, on David’s throne, and on his kingdom, to establish it, and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from that time on, even forever. The zeal of Yahweh of Armies will perform this.
verses.8: The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it falls on Israel.
verses.9: All the people will know, including Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria, who say in pride and in arrogance of heart,
verses.10: “The bricks have fallen, but we will build with cut stone. The sycamore fig trees have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place.”
verses.11: Therefore Yahweh will set up on high against him the adversaries of Rezin, and will stir up his enemies,
verses.12: The Syrians in front, and the Philistines behind; and they will devour Israel with open mouth. For all this, his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.13: Yet the people have not turned to him who struck them, neither have they sought Yahweh of Armies.
verses.14: Therefore Yahweh will cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, in one day.
verses.15: The elder and the honorable man is the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
verses.16: For those who lead this people lead them astray; and those who are led by them are destroyed.
verses.17: Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over their young men, neither will he have compassion on their fatherless and widows; for everyone is profane and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks folly. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.18: For wickedness burns like a fire. It devours the briers and thorns; yes, it kindles in the thickets of the forest, and they roll upward in a column of smoke.
verses.19: Through Yahweh of Armies’ wrath, the land is burned up; and the people are the fuel for the fire. No one spares his brother.
verses.20: One will devour on the right hand, and be hungry; and he will eat on the left hand, and they will not be satisfied. Everyone will eat the flesh of his own arm:
verses.21: Manasseh eating Ephraim and Ephraim eating Manasseh, and they together will be against Judah. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

verses.1: Listen, islands, to me. Listen, you peoples, from afar: Yahweh has called me from the womb; from the inside of my mother, he has mentioned my name.
verses.2: He has made my mouth like a sharp sword. He has hidden me in the shadow of his hand. He has made me a polished shaft. He has kept me close in his quiver.
verses.3: He said to me, “You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified.”
verses.4: But I said, “I have labored in vain. I have spent my strength in vain for nothing; yet surely the justice due to me is with Yahweh, and my reward with my God.”
verses.5: Now Yahweh, he who formed me from the womb to be his servant, says to bring Jacob again to him, and to gather Israel to him, for I am honorable in Yahweh’s eyes, and my God has become my strength.
verses.6: Indeed, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel. I will also give you as a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.”
verses.7: Yahweh, the Redeemer of Israel, and his Holy One, says to him whom man despises, to him whom the nation abhors, to a servant of rulers: “Kings shall see and rise up, princes, and they shall worship, because of Yahweh who is faithful, even the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you.”
verses.8: Yahweh says, “I have answered you in an acceptable time. I have helped you in a day of salvation. I will preserve you and give you for a covenant of the people, to raise up the land, to make them inherit the desolate heritage,
verses.9: saying to those who are bound, ‘Come out!’; to those who are in darkness, ‘Show yourselves!’ “They shall feed along the paths, and their pasture shall be on all treeless heights.
verses.10: They shall not hunger nor thirst; neither shall the heat nor sun strike them, for he who has mercy on them will lead them. He will guide them by springs of water.
verses.11: I will make all my mountains a road, and my highways shall be exalted.
verses.12: Behold, these shall come from afar, and behold, these from the north and from the west, and these from the land of Sinim.”
verses.13: Sing, heavens, and be joyful, earth! Break out into singing, mountains! For Yahweh has comforted his people, and will have compassion on his afflicted.
verses.14: But Zion said, “Yahweh has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me.”
verses.15: “Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? Yes, these may forget, yet I will not forget you!
verses.16: Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands. Your walls are continually before me.
verses.17: Your children hurry. Your destroyers and those who devastated you will leave you.
verses.18: Lift up your eyes all around, and see: all these gather themselves together, and come to you. As I live,” says Yahweh, “you shall surely clothe yourself with them all as with an ornament, and dress yourself with them, like a bride.
verses.19: “For, as for your waste and your desolate places, and your land that has been destroyed, surely now that land will be too small for the inhabitants, and those who swallowed you up will be far away.
verses.20: The children of your bereavement will say in your ears, ‘This place is too small for me. Give me a place to live in.’
verses.21: Then you will say in your heart, ‘Who has conceived these for me, since I have been bereaved of my children and am alone, an exile, and wandering back and forth? Who has brought these up? Behold, I was left alone. Where were these?’ ”
verses.22: The Lord Yahweh says, “Behold, I will lift up my hand to the nations, and lift up my banner to the peoples. They shall bring your sons in their bosom, and your daughters shall be carried on their shoulders.
verses.23: Kings shall be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They will bow down to you with their faces to the earth, and lick the dust of your feet. Then you will know that I am Yahweh; and those who wait for me won’t be disappointed.”
verses.24: Shall the plunder be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captives be delivered?
verses.25: But Yahweh says, “Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the plunder retrieved from the fierce, for I will contend with him who contends with you and I will save your children.
verses.26: I will feed those who oppress you with their own flesh; and they will be drunk on their own blood, as with sweet wine. Then all flesh shall know that I, Yahweh, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.”

verses.1: Since many have undertaken to set in order a narrative concerning those matters which have been fulfilled among us,
verses.2: even as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word delivered them to us,
verses.3: it seemed good to me also, having traced the course of all things accurately from the first, to write to you in order, most excellent Theophilus;
verses.4: that you might know the certainty concerning the things in which you were instructed.
verses.5: There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the priestly division of Abijah. He had a wife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
verses.6: They were both righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord.
verses.7: But they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and they both were well advanced in years.
verses.8: Now while he executed the priest’s office before God in the order of his division
verses.9: according to the custom of the priest’s office, his lot was to enter into the temple of the Lord and burn incense.
verses.10: The whole multitude of the people were praying outside at the hour of incense.
verses.11: An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
verses.12: Zacharias was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.
verses.13: But the angel said to him, “Don’t be afraid, Zacharias, because your request has been heard. Your wife, Elizabeth, will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.
verses.14: You will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth.
verses.15: For he will be great in the sight of the Lord, and he will drink no wine nor strong drink. He will be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother’s womb.
verses.16: He will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God.
verses.17: He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, ‘to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children,’ and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to prepare a people prepared for the Lord.”
verses.18: Zacharias said to the angel, “How can I be sure of this? For I am an old man, and my wife is well advanced in years.”
verses.19: The angel answered him, “I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God. I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.
verses.20: Behold, you will be silent and not able to speak until the day that these things will happen, because you didn’t believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their proper time.”
verses.21: The people were waiting for Zacharias, and they marveled that he delayed in the temple.
verses.22: When he came out, he could not speak to them. They perceived that he had seen a vision in the temple. He continued making signs to them, and remained mute.
verses.23: When the days of his service were fulfilled, he departed to his house.
verses.24: After these days Elizabeth his wife conceived, and she hid herself five months, saying,
verses.25: “Thus has the Lord done to me in the days in which he looked at me, to take away my reproach among men.”
verses.26: Now in the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth,
verses.27: to a virgin pledged to be married to a man whose name was Joseph, of David’s house. The virgin’s name was Mary.
verses.28: Having come in, the angel said to her, “Rejoice, you highly favored one! The Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women!”
verses.29: But when she saw him, she was greatly troubled at the saying, and considered what kind of salutation this might be.
verses.30: The angel said to her, “Don’t be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
verses.31: Behold, you will conceive in your womb and give birth to a son, and shall name him ‘Jesus.’
verses.32: He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David,
verses.33: and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever. There will be no end to his Kingdom.”
verses.34: Mary said to the angel, “How can this be, seeing I am a virgin?”
verses.35: The angel answered her, “The Holy Spirit will come on you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore also the holy one who is born from you will be called the Son of God.
verses.36: Behold, Elizabeth your relative also has conceived a son in her old age; and this is the sixth month with her who was called barren.
verses.37: For nothing spoken by God is impossible.”
verses.38: Mary said, “Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.” Then the angel departed from her.
verses.39: Mary arose in those days and went into the hill country with haste, into a city of Judah,
verses.40: and entered into the house of Zacharias and greeted Elizabeth.
verses.41: When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb; and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
verses.42: She called out with a loud voice and said, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
verses.43: Why am I so favored, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
verses.44: For behold, when the voice of your greeting came into my ears, the baby leaped in my womb for joy!
verses.45: Blessed is she who believed, for there will be a fulfillment of the things which have been spoken to her from the Lord!”
verses.46: Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord.
verses.47: My spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,
verses.48: for he has looked at the humble state of his servant. For behold, from now on, all generations will call me blessed.
verses.49: For he who is mighty has done great things for me. Holy is his name.
verses.50: His mercy is for generations and generations on those who fear him.
verses.51: He has shown strength with his arm. He has scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts.
verses.52: He has put down princes from their thrones, and has exalted the lowly.
verses.53: He has filled the hungry with good things. He has sent the rich away empty.
verses.54: He has given help to Israel, his servant, that he might remember mercy,
verses.55: as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his offspring forever.”
verses.56: Mary stayed with her about three months, and then returned to her house.
verses.57: Now the time that Elizabeth should give birth was fulfilled, and she gave birth to a son.
verses.58: Her neighbors and her relatives heard that the Lord had magnified his mercy toward her, and they rejoiced with her.
verses.59: On the eighth day, they came to circumcise the child; and they would have called him Zacharias, after the name of his father.
verses.60: His mother answered, “Not so; but he will be called John.”
verses.61: They said to her, “There is no one among your relatives who is called by this name.”
verses.62: They made signs to his father, what he would have him called.
verses.63: He asked for a writing tablet, and wrote, “His name is John.” They all marveled.
verses.64: His mouth was opened immediately and his tongue freed, and he spoke, blessing God.
verses.65: Fear came on all who lived around them, and all these sayings were talked about throughout all the hill country of Judea.
verses.66: All who heard them laid them up in their heart, saying, “What then will this child be?” The hand of the Lord was with him.
verses.67: His father Zacharias was filled with the Holy Spirit, and prophesied, saying,
verses.68: “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, for he has visited and redeemed his people;
verses.69: and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David
verses.70: (as he spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets who have been from of old),
verses.71: salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us;
verses.72: to show mercy toward our fathers, to remember his holy covenant,
verses.73: the oath which he swore to Abraham our father,
verses.74: to grant to us that we, being delivered out of the hand of our enemies, should serve him without fear,
verses.75: in holiness and righteousness before him all the days of our life.
verses.76: And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways,
verses.77: to give knowledge of salvation to his people by the remission of their sins,
verses.78: because of the tender mercy of our God, by which the dawn from on high will visit us,
verses.79: to shine on those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death; to guide our feet into the way of peace.”
verses.80: The child was growing and becoming strong in spirit, and was in the desert until the day of his public appearance to Israel.

verses.1: Now in those days, a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be enrolled.
verses.2: This was the first enrollment made when Quirinius was governor of Syria.
verses.3: All went to enroll themselves, everyone to his own city.
verses.4: Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to David’s city, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David,
verses.5: to enroll himself with Mary, who was pledged to be married to him as wife, being pregnant.
verses.6: While they were there, the day had come for her to give birth.
verses.7: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.
verses.8: There were shepherds in the same country staying in the field, and keeping watch by night over their flock.
verses.9: Behold, an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.
verses.10: The angel said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people.
verses.11: For there is born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
verses.12: This is the sign to you: you will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth, lying in a feeding trough.”
verses.13: Suddenly, there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army praising God and saying,
verses.14: “Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace, good will toward men.”
verses.15: When the angels went away from them into the sky, the shepherds said to one another, “Let’s go to Bethlehem, now, and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
verses.16: They came with haste and found both Mary and Joseph, and the baby was lying in the feeding trough.
verses.17: When they saw it, they publicized widely the saying which was spoken to them about this child.
verses.18: All who heard it wondered at the things which were spoken to them by the shepherds.
verses.19: But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.
verses.20: The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, just as it was told them.
verses.21: When eight days were fulfilled for the circumcision of the child, his name was called Jesus, which was given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
verses.22: When the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were fulfilled, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord
verses.23: (as it is written in the law of the Lord, “Every male who opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord”),
verses.24: and to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, “A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.”
verses.25: Behold, there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon. This man was righteous and devout, looking for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was on him.
verses.26: It had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he should not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
verses.27: He came in the Spirit into the temple. When the parents brought in the child, Jesus, that they might do concerning him according to the custom of the law,
verses.28: then he received him into his arms and blessed God, and said,
verses.29: “Now you are releasing your servant, Master, according to your word, in peace;
verses.30: for my eyes have seen your salvation,
verses.31: which you have prepared before the face of all peoples;
verses.32: a light for revelation to the nations, and the glory of your people Israel.”
verses.33: Joseph and his mother were marveling at the things which were spoken concerning him.
verses.34: Simeon blessed them, and said to Mary, his mother, “Behold, this child is appointed for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and for a sign which is spoken against.
verses.35: Yes, a sword will pierce through your own soul, that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”
verses.36: There was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher (she was of a great age, having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity,
verses.37: and she had been a widow for about eighty-four years), who didn’t depart from the temple, worshiping with fastings and petitions night and day.
verses.38: Coming up at that very hour, she gave thanks to the Lord, and spoke of him to all those who were looking for redemption in Jerusalem.
verses.39: When they had accomplished all things that were according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city, Nazareth.
verses.40: The child was growing, and was becoming strong in spirit, being filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.
verses.41: His parents went every year to Jerusalem at the feast of the Passover.
verses.42: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;
verses.43: and when they had fulfilled the days, as they were returning, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. Joseph and his mother didn’t know it,
verses.44: but supposing him to be in the company, they went a day’s journey; and they looked for him among their relatives and acquaintances.
verses.45: When they didn’t find him, they returned to Jerusalem, looking for him.
verses.46: After three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the middle of the teachers, both listening to them and asking them questions.
verses.47: All who heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
verses.48: When they saw him, they were astonished; and his mother said to him, “Son, why have you treated us this way? Behold, your father and I were anxiously looking for you.”
verses.49: He said to them, “Why were you looking for me? Didn’t you know that I must be in my Father’s house?”
verses.50: They didn’t understand the saying which he spoke to them.
verses.51: And he went down with them and came to Nazareth. He was subject to them, and his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.
verses.52: And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.

verses.1: Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
verses.2: during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John, the son of Zacharias, in the wilderness.
verses.3: He came into all the region around the Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for remission of sins.
verses.4: As it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make ready the way of the Lord. Make his paths straight.
verses.5: Every valley will be filled. Every mountain and hill will be brought low. The crooked will become straight, and the rough ways smooth.
verses.6: All flesh will see God’s salvation.’ ”
verses.7: He said therefore to the multitudes who went out to be baptized by him, “You offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
verses.8: Therefore produce fruits worthy of repentance, and don’t begin to say among yourselves, ‘We have Abraham for our father;’ for I tell you that God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones!
verses.9: Even now the ax also lies at the root of the trees. Every tree therefore that doesn’t produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.”
verses.10: The multitudes asked him, “What then must we do?”
verses.11: He answered them, “He who has two coats, let him give to him who has none. He who has food, let him do likewise.”
verses.12: Tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they said to him, “Teacher, what must we do?”
verses.13: He said to them, “Collect no more than that which is appointed to you.”
verses.14: Soldiers also asked him, saying, “What about us? What must we do?” He said to them, “Extort from no one by violence, neither accuse anyone wrongfully. Be content with your wages.”
verses.15: As the people were in expectation, and all men reasoned in their hearts concerning John, whether perhaps he was the Christ,
verses.16: John answered them all, “I indeed baptize you with water, but he comes who is mightier than I, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to loosen. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire.
verses.17: His winnowing fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor, and will gather the wheat into his barn; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”
verses.18: Then with many other exhortations he preached good news to the people,
verses.19: but Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him for Herodias, his brother’s wife, and for all the evil things which Herod had done,
verses.20: added this also to them all, that he shut up John in prison.
verses.21: Now when all the people were baptized, Jesus also had been baptized and was praying. The sky was opened,
verses.22: and the Holy Spirit descended in a bodily form like a dove on him; and a voice came out of the sky, saying “You are my beloved Son. In you I am well pleased.”
verses.23: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,
verses.24: the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
verses.25: the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai,
verses.26: the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Joseph, the son of Judah,
verses.27: the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri,
verses.28: the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmodam, the son of Er,
verses.29: the son of Jose, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,
verses.30: the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonan, the son of Eliakim,
verses.31: the son of Melea, the son of Menan, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,
verses.32: the son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Salmon, the son of Nahshon,
verses.33: the son of Amminadab, the son of Aram, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,
verses.34: the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,
verses.35: the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
verses.36: the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,
verses.37: the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalaleel, the son of Cainan,
verses.38: the son of Enos, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.

verses.1: Now you shall gather yourself in troops, daughter of troops. He has laid siege against us. They will strike the judge of Israel with a rod on the cheek.
verses.2: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, being small among the clans of Judah, out of you one will come out to me who is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings out are from of old, from ancient times.
verses.3: Therefore he will abandon them until the time that she who is in labor gives birth. Then the rest of his brothers will return to the children of Israel.
verses.4: He shall stand, and shall shepherd in the strength of Yahweh, in the majesty of the name of Yahweh his God. They will live, for then he will be great to the ends of the earth.
verses.5: He will be our peace when Assyria invades our land and when he marches through our fortresses, then we will raise against him seven shepherds, and eight leaders of men.
verses.6: They will rule the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in its gates. He will deliver us from the Assyrian, when he invades our land, and when he marches within our border.
verses.7: The remnant of Jacob will be among many peoples like dew from Yahweh, like showers on the grass, that don’t wait for man nor wait for the sons of men.
verses.8: The remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, among many peoples, like a lion among the animals of the forest, like a young lion among the flocks of sheep; who, if he goes through, treads down and tears in pieces, and there is no one to deliver.
verses.9: Let your hand be lifted up above your adversaries, and let all of your enemies be cut off.
verses.10: “It will happen in that day”, says Yahweh, “that I will cut off your horses from among you and will destroy your chariots.
verses.11: I will cut off the cities of your land and will tear down all your strongholds.
verses.12: I will destroy witchcraft from your hand. You shall have no soothsayers.
verses.13: I will cut off your engraved images and your pillars from among you; and you shall no more worship the work of your hands.
verses.14: I will uproot your Asherah poles from among you; and I will destroy your cities.
verses.15: I will execute vengeance in anger and wrath on the nations that didn’t listen.”
